questions.question: Which tag creates a bulleted list?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <ul> creates an unordered list (bulleted list). "ul" stands for "unordered list" - items don't have a specific sequence.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <ul> creates an unordered list (bulleted list). "ul" stands for "unordered list" - items don't have a specific sequence.

questions.question: Which tag creates a numbered list?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <ol> creates an ordered list (numbered list). "ol" stands for "ordered list" - items have a specific sequence or ranking.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <ol> creates an ordered list (numbered list). "ol" stands for "ordered list" - items have a specific sequence or ranking.

questions.question: What tag defines each list item?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <li> defines list items inside both <ul> and <ol>. "li" stands for "list item" - each bullet or number is an <li>.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <li> defines list items inside both <ul> and <ol>. "li" stands for "list item" - each bullet or number is an <li>.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Proper structure: <ul> (list container) wraps <li> (list items). <li> tags must be direct children of <ul> or <ol>.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Proper structure: <ul> (list container) wraps <li> (list items). <li> tags must be direct children of <ul> or <ol>.

questions.question: To create a list: A, B, C... use:

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <ol type="A"> creates uppercase alphabetical numbering. Other types: 1 (numbers), a (lowercase letters), I (Roman numerals).

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <ol type="A"> creates uppercase alphabetical numbering. Other types: 1 (numbers), a (lowercase letters), I (Roman numerals).

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <li> tags can appear inside either <ul> (unordered) or <ol> (ordered) lists. They define individual list items in any list type.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <li> tags can appear inside either <ul> (unordered) or <ol> (ordered) lists. They define individual list items in any list type.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Nested lists are lists inside list items. You put a new <ul> or <ol> inside an <li> to create sub-lists.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Nested lists are lists inside list items. You put a new <ul> or <ol> inside an <li> to create sub-lists.

questions.question: Which creates a list starting at 5?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <ol start="5"> makes the list start at 5. Useful for continuing numbered lists across pages or sections.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <ol start="5"> makes the list start at 5. Useful for continuing numbered lists across pages or sections.

questions.question: For a list of features with no order, use:

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Use <ul> (unordered list) for items without specific order - like features, ingredients, or bullet points.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Use <ul> (unordered list) for items without specific order - like features, ingredients, or bullet points.

questions.question: Which is good for a recipe's steps?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Use <ol> (ordered list) for sequential steps - like recipe instructions where order matters.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Use <ol> (ordered list) for sequential steps - like recipe instructions where order matters.
